practiceQuestions.q: Who nominates the members of the Panel of Chairpersons in the Lok Sabha?
opts: The President of India
The Prime Minister of India
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the Speaker nominates from among the members a panel of chairpersons. Hence, option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the typical maximum number of members nominated to the Panel of Chairpersons in the Lok Sabha?
opts: Not more than 5
Not more than 10
Exactly 15
Not fixed by any rules
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Rules of Procedure of Lok Sabha, the Speaker nominates a panel of not more than ten chairpersons from among the members. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Under what circumstance does a member of the Panel of Chairpersons preside over the Lok Sabha?
opts: When the Prime Minister is absent
When both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent
When the President addresses the joint sitting
During the election of the Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: A member of the panel of chairpersons can preside over the House only when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent from a sitting of the House. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of the Panel of Chairpersons preside over the Lok Sabha when the office of the Speaker is vacant?
opts: Yes, always
No, a member of the panel cannot preside when the office of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is vacant
Yes, with the permission of the Supreme Court
Yes, if appointed by the President as Pro Tem Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: The panel of chairpersons cannot preside when the office of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker is vacant. During such a vacancy, the Speaker's duties are performed by the Speaker Pro Tem or a member appointed by the President. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following powers can a member of the Panel of Chairpersons NOT exercise while presiding over the Lok Sabha?
opts: Ruling on points of order
Allowing a motion for adjournment
Having the same powers as the Speaker while presiding
Holding a substantive election to choose a permanent Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: While presiding, a member of the panel has all the powers of the Speaker. However, a member of the panel CANNOT preside when the office of the Speaker is vacant, meaning they do not conduct the election of a permanent Speaker (which requires a Speaker Pro Tem or vacancy provisions). Hence, option D is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of the members of the Panel of Chairpersons in the Lok Sabha?
opts: Entire 5 years term of the Lok Sabha
1 year
Until a new panel is nominated
Until the next session of Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: Members of the Panel of Chairpersons hold office until a new panel is nominated. They are typically nominated for the duration of the Lok Sabha or until the Speaker reconstitutes the panel. Hence, option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Does a member of the Panel of Chairpersons receive any special salary or allowances solely for being on the panel?
opts: Yes, equal to the salary of the Deputy Speaker
Yes, a monthly honorarium fixed by the Speaker
No, they draw only the normal salary and allowances of a Member of Parliament
Yes, equal to the salary of a Union Cabinet Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: Members of the panel of chairpersons do not receive any additional salary or special allowances simply by virtue of being on the panel, though they may receive allowances when actually presiding if specified, but traditionally they draw MP salary. Hence, option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Where are the rules regarding the Panel of Chairpersons primarily laid down?
opts: Article 93 of the Constitution of India
Article 100 of the Constitution of India
Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha
The Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953
practiceQuestions.sol: The Panel of Chairpersons is an institutional mechanism created under the internal Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, rather than being explicitly detailed in the Constitution text. Hence, option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: When a member of the Panel of Chairpersons is presiding over the House, does he/she have the right to vote in the first instance?
opts: Yes, always
No, like the Speaker, he/she can only exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie
Yes, but only on Money Bills
No, he/she loses all voting rights permanently
practiceQuestions.sol: While presiding, a member of the panel exercises the same powers as the Speaker. Therefore, they do not vote in the first instance and can only exercise a casting vote in the event of a tie. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies/offices shares a similar structural concept of a panel of presiding officers in the Rajya Sabha?
opts: Panel of Vice-Chairpersons of Rajya Sabha
Panel of Whips of Rajya Sabha
Rules Committee of Rajya Sabha
General Purposes Committee
practiceQuestions.sol: Similar to the Lok Sabha's Panel of Chairpersons, the Rajya Sabha has a 'Panel of Vice-Chairpersons' nominated by the Chairman from among the members to preside in the absence of both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman. Hence, option A is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Panel of Chairpersons considered a crucial procedural innovation rather than a constitutional mandate?
opts: Because it is mandated by a constitutional amendment enacted under Article 368
Because the Constitution provides only for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, leaving operational continuity in absences to internal parliamentary rules
Because it overrides the constitutional powers of the President
Because it completely replaces the Deputy Speaker during emergencies
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Constitution explicitly establishes the offices of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker under Article 93, but it does not mention a panel of chairpersons. To ensure uninterrupted functioning of the House when both dignitaries are absent, the Lok Sabha created this panel via its internal Rules of Procedure. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the functioning of the Panel of Chairpersons reflect the principle of continuous institutional continuity in parliamentary democracy?
opts: By allowing non-elected bureaucrats to run legislative debates
By ensuring that legislative proceedings do not halt due to the simultaneous absence or illness of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker
By granting supreme judicial veto power to senior MPs
By permitting executive interference in parliamentary voting
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliamentary democracy requires uninterrupted legislative output and oversight. If the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are both unavailable, having a ready panel of experienced members prevents adjournment or paralysis of the House, exemplifying institutional continuity. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication if the office of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker falls vacant simultaneously, regarding the Panel of Chairpersons?
opts: The senior-most member of the Panel of Chairpersons automatically becomes the Speaker
The panel members can jointly elect one among themselves to act as Speaker indefinitely
The panel cannot function or preside, and duties must be fulfilled as per provisions for vacancy under Article 95(1) via Speaker Pro Tem / President's appointment
The Prime Minister assumes the role of Lok Sabha Speaker temporarily

practiceQuestions.q: Why are members from diverse political parties typically included in the Panel of Chairpersons?
opts: To fulfill mandatory constitutional quotas for regional parties
To foster political neutrality, bipartisanship, and smooth conduct of the House across party lines
To dilute the absolute powers of the ruling party's Speaker
To bypass the necessity of having a Deputy Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: Inclusion of members from various parties in the Panel of Chairpersons promotes bipartisan consensus, ensures impartial rulings that are respected by all factions, and upholds the dignity of the Chair. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a member of the Panel of Chairpersons be removed or replaced by the Speaker during the tenure of the Lok Sabha?
opts: No, once nominated, they cannot be removed until the Lok Sabha is dissolved
Yes, the Speaker can reconstitute or modify the panel at any time
Yes, but only with a two-thirds majority resolution passed by the Lok Sabha
No, removal requires the recommendation of the Privileges Committee
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Speaker nominates the panel under internal rules, the Speaker retains the administrative authority to reconstitute, add, or replace members on the panel as and when required. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: In terms of hierarchy and protocol, how does a member of the Panel of Chairpersons rank when NOT presiding over the House?
opts: They hold a special cabinet rank in the Table of Precedence
They maintain the exact same rank as any other ordinary Member of Parliament in the Table of Precedence
They rank immediately below the Deputy Speaker in official state protocol
They rank above all Union Ministers
practiceQuestions.sol: Being on the panel of chairpersons does not alter a member's standing in the national Table of Precedence when they are not in the chair; they remain ordinary MPs in terms of general protocol. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: What distinguishes the role of the Panel of Chairpersons from that of the Speaker Pro Tem?
opts: The Speaker Pro Tem administers oaths to new MPs and oversees the election of the Speaker, whereas the Panel of Chairpersons presides over routine sittings in the absence of the Speaker/Deputy Speaker
The Panel of Chairpersons is a permanent constitutional office, while Speaker Pro Tem is temporary
Speaker Pro Tem is chosen by the Supreme Court, while the panel is chosen by the Prime Minister
There is no functional distinction; both perform identical duties simultaneously
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker Pro Tem is a temporary office specifically for swearing in new members and conducting the election of the Speaker. The Panel of Chairpersons functions throughout the life of the Lok Sabha to preside during regular sittings when principal officers are absent. Hence, option C is incorrect and option A is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: If a member of the Panel of Chairpersons makes a ruling on a procedural matter while presiding, can it be easily challenged or reversed by the substantive Speaker upon return?
opts: Yes, the Speaker routinely reverses all panel rulings as a matter of administrative review
No, while presiding, the panel member exercises full authority of the Chair, and their rulings hold standard institutional validity
Yes, because panel rulings require judicial ratification to be valid
No one can ever challenge a panel ruling, not even the Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: While presiding, a member of the panel exercises the powers of the Speaker, and their rulings carry the same weight and validity as those of the Speaker. They are not arbitrarily overturned upon the Speaker's return. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the selection process of the Panel of Chairpersons underline the administrative autonomy of the Lok Sabha Speaker?
opts: It requires the executive cabinet to vet and approve every name
It is done solely by the Speaker without requiring formal executive clearance or floor voting
It is managed by the Election Commission of India
It must be ratified by a joint sitting of both Houses
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker has absolute discretionary power under the Rules of Procedure to nominate the panel without needing approval from the government or a parliamentary motion, demonstrating the independent authority of the Speaker's office. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind setting a limit of up to ten members on the Panel of Chairpersons?
opts: To restrict public expenditure on Parliament
To ensure a broad enough pool of capable presiding officers for continuous house sittings while maintaining quality and familiarity with rules
To match the exact number of ministries in the Union Cabinet
To comply with international parliamentary union standards
practiceQuestions.sol: Having a panel of up to ten members ensures that multiple qualified individuals are available across long or simultaneous committee meetings and house shifts, preventing disruptions when both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are occupied. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Panel of Chairpersons of Lok Sabha:
1. The members of the panel are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
2. A member of the panel can preside over the House even when the office of the Speaker is vacant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Speaker nominates a panel of chairpersons from among the members. Statement 2 is incorrect: A member of the panel cannot preside when the office of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker is vacant. Hence, option A is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The maximum number of members on the Panel of Chairpersons of Lok Sabha is fixed at ten by the Constitution of India.
2. When presiding over the House, a member of the panel has the same powers as the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the limit of up to ten members is fixed by the internal Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, not directly by the Constitution text. Statement 2 is correct: while presiding, a panel member exercises all powers of the Speaker. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the absence of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker:
1. In the absence of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, any member of the Panel of Chairpersons can preside over the Lok Sabha.
2. If no member of the Panel of Chairpersons is present, the House may choose any other member as determined by the House to preside.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under the rules of Lok Sabha, when both Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent, a member from the panel of chairpersons presides. If no panel member is available, the House elects another member to preside for that sitting. Hence, option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Panel of Chairpersons:
1. Members of the Panel of Chairpersons draw a special higher salary comparable to that of a Union Minister while they are on the panel.
2. The panel ceases to exist automatically upon the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because members of the panel do not receive any additional salary or allowance just for being on the panel; they receive normal MP salaries. Statement 2 is correct: since the Lok Sabha dissolves, the panel appointed for that House also lapses. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of a presiding member of the Panel of Chairpersons:
1. A member of the panel can vote in the first instance on any bill before exercising a casting vote.
2. A ruling given by a panel member on a point of order cannot be questioned or challenged during that sitting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because while presiding, the member acts in place of the Speaker and therefore does not vote in the first instance (only exercises a casting vote in case of a tie). Statement 2 is correct: rulings on points of order by the chair are final for that sitting. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The provisions establishing the Panel of Chairpersons are explicitly outlined under Article 118 of the Constitution of India.
2. Rajya Sabha has a corresponding institutional mechanism known as the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 118 empowers each House of Parliament to make rules for regulating its procedure, but the specific Panel of Chairpersons is detailed in the internal Rules of Procedure of Lok Sabha, not directly as a constitutional article text. Statement 2 is correct: Rajya Sabha has a Panel of Vice-Chairpersons. Hence, option B is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal or reconstitution of the Panel of Chairpersons:
1. The Speaker can remove any member from the panel or add new members at any time.
2. A resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of Lok Sabha is required to remove a member from the Panel of Chairpersons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct because nomination and reconstitution of the panel is entirely at the discretion of the Speaker. Statement 2 is incorrect; no parliamentary resolution is required to modify or remove members from the administrative panel. Hence, option A is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary presiding officers:
1. The Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is subordinate to the Speaker in administrative terms.
2. Members of the Panel of Chairpersons rank higher than the Deputy Speaker when presiding over the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker in terms of independence of office (elected by the House), but in administrative allocation of work, the Speaker assigns responsibilities. Statement 2 is incorrect: when presiding, a panel member exercises the powers of the chair, but they do not outrank the Deputy Speaker in constitutional hierarchy or protocol status. Hence, option A is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding legislative practices in India:
1. The practice of having a panel of chairpersons is unique to the Lok Sabha and has no parallel in State Legislative Assemblies.
2. A member of the Panel of Chairpersons can sign and authenticate bills passed by Lok Sabha if authorized during specific absences of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because State Legislative Assemblies also have similar panels of chairpersons appointed by their respective Speakers under state assembly rules. Statement 2 is incorrect because authenticating bills and certifying Money Bills are constitutional/statutory duties specifically reserved for the Speaker (or Deputy Speaker under specific constitutional provisions), not routinely delegated to temporary panel members. Hence, option D is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The composition of the Panel of Chairpersons reflects representation from various political parties in the Lok Sabha.
2. A member of the Panel of Chairpersons retains their membership in parliamentary committees while presiding over the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 is correct because Speakers traditionally appoint members from ruling and opposition parties to ensure broad acceptability. Statement 2 is correct because serving on the panel of chairpersons is a part-time rotational duty; members continue to hold their regular MP status, committee memberships, and party affiliations. Hence, option C is correct.
